literal: When the five ranks were newly established, his fief was two thousand households.
idiomatic: When the five ranks were first set up, his fief stood at two thousand households.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he took charge as Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign he served as Grand Marshal.

literal: Gaozu personally led the armies; he encountered Xiu with three thieves paraded before the six armies, about to be executed, when an edict pardoned them.
idiomatic: Gaozu was leading the armies in person when Xiu had three thieves displayed before the host and was about to execute them; an edict then pardoned them.

literal: Xiu held fast and said: "Your Majesty is about to go far and clear Heng and Huo; therefore you personally lead the six armies, tramping through the wilds. The march has only just begun and already there are thieves. If they are not beheaded, how can theft be stilled? I beg that the punishment be carried out without fail, to awe the wicked.
idiomatic: Xiu pressed his case: "Your Majesty means to go far and clear Heng and Huo, and so leads the six armies yourself through the wilds. The march has barely begun and thieves already appear. If they are not beheaded, how will theft cease? I beg that the sentence be carried out, to awe the wicked.

literal: " The edict said: "The Grand Marshal holds the law—indeed it should be so.
idiomatic: " The throne answered: "The Grand Marshal holds the law—so it should be.

literal: But by chance of circumstance I have heard that the body of a king also at times grants an extraordinary grace; though it violates military law, they may be specially spared.
idiomatic: Yet chance has put me here, and I have heard that a king's body may at times grant an extraordinary grace; though this breaks military law, let them be specially spared.

literal: " Xiu then received the edict.
idiomatic: " Xiu then obeyed the edict.

literal: Gaozu said to the Minister of Education Feng Dan: "The Grand Marshal is stern and holds to the law; the armies cannot but be careful.
idiomatic: Gaozu told Minister of Education Feng Dan: "The Grand Marshal is stern and holds the law—the armies had better take care.

literal: " Thereupon the six armies were in awe.
idiomatic: " After that the six armies stood in awe.

literal: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Xiu followed the imperial progress to Ye.
idiomatic: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Xiu followed the court to Ye.

literal: He was ordered to lead the civil and military who followed the progress and bring the household from Pingcheng.
idiomatic: He was ordered to lead the civil and military of the progress and bring the household down from Pingcheng.

literal: Gaozu personally saw Xiu off north of the Zhang River.
idiomatic: Gaozu personally saw him off north of the Zhang River.

literal: In the eighteenth year Xiu lay ill in bed; Gaozu visited his residence, wept and inquired after his illness, and palace envoys with medicine followed one another along the road.
idiomatic: In year 18 Xiu took to his bed; Gaozu came to his house, wept, and asked after him, while palace envoys with medicine crowded the road.

literal: He died; funeral gifts were three thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: He died; funeral gifts were three thousand bolts of silk.

literal: From death until the encoffining the imperial carriage came three times.
idiomatic: From his death to encoffining the emperor came three times.

literal: Gaozu came to his gate, changed dress and granted hemp mourning, [10] plain cap with hemp band.
idiomatic: Gaozu came to his gate, changed into mourning dress and granted hemp, [10] with plain cap and hemp band.

literal: The crown prince and the hundred officials all followed in performing mourning rites.
idiomatic: The crown prince and all officials followed in the mourning rites.

literal: When the time came to bury, two thousand more bolts of silk were granted; posthumous title: Prince Jing.
idiomatic: At burial two thousand more bolts of silk were granted; posthumous title: Prince Jing.

literal: An edict lent the yellow battle-axe, added feather canopy, guard music, tiger guards, and sixty-three sword-bearers of the imperial guard—all matching the rites for the Three Elders, Yuan Yuan.
idiomatic: An edict lent the yellow axe, with feather canopy, guard music, tiger guards, and sixty-three imperial sword-bearers—all matching the rites for the Three Elders Yuan Yuan.

literal: Gaozu personally escorted him beyond the suburbs, wept and returned, and no prince received such favor in mourning.
idiomatic: Gaozu escorted him beyond the suburbs, wept on his return, and no prince was ever mourned with such honor.

literal: In Shizong's time he was given a place in the temple sacrifices.
idiomatic: Under Shizong he was given a place in the ancestral temple.

literal: Eldest son: An
idiomatic: Eldest son: An

literal: The eldest son An died young.
idiomatic: The eldest son An died in childhood.

literal: Second son: Xie
idiomatic: Second son: Xie

literal: The second son Xie was made Lower Grand Master.
idiomatic: The second son Xie was made lower grand master.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he inherited and was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Hua Province.
idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne he inherited and was made grand master of the palace, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Hua inspector.

literal: Xie memorialized, saying: "I respectfully consider the seat of Zhou prefecture at Li Run Fort: though it is the old ground of Lesser Liang and the fief-grant of Jin and Rui, yet with Hu and Yi submitting within, it has become a barbarian settlement.
idiomatic: Xie submitted a memorial: "I have weighed the seat of Zhou prefecture at Li Run Fort. It lies on old Lesser Liang ground and on Jin and Rui's grant, but once the Hu and Yi came in it turned into a barbarian quarter.

literal: The city is not an old town's name of former generations; from the founding of the state it was a small garrison protecting the Qiang.
idiomatic: The town bears no ancient name from earlier ages; from the dynasty's founding it was only a small garrison guarding the Qiang.

literal: When the garrison was changed to a commandery and a prefecture set up on the model of a mountain, the name and reality were never carved in the registers of the granary offices.
idiomatic: When the post became a commandery and a prefecture was raised on a mountain model, name and fact were never fixed in the granary registers.

literal: I see the old city of Fengyi: where the Qiang and Wei peoples meet, on the water and land route between Xu and Luo—a left-hand guard of Former Han, the right wing of august Wei, a stronghold and famous capital, truly the inner treasury of the western border.
idiomatic: I look at the old city of Fengyi, where Qiang and Wei meet, on the water road between Xu and Luo—Former Han's left-hand guard, august Wei's right wing, a fortress and famous capital, truly the inner treasury of the western marches.

literal: Where the prefecture now sits is not only not the old site; it even dwells on hills and drinks from ravines, wells and valleys foul and mixed, climbing and descending toilsome, coming and going several li.
idiomatic: Where the prefecture sits now is not merely off the old site; people live on ridges, drink from gullies, wells and lanes are foul and tangled, and every trip up or down costs miles of labor.

literal: Noise and clamor from dawn to dusk injure ritual and teaching.
idiomatic: Noise from dawn to dusk mars ritual and teaching.

literal: It is not like Fengyi, facing Hua and Wei, embracing plains and marshes, with shallow wells and level pools, firewood and pasture ample.
idiomatic: Fengyi faces Hua and Wei, holds plains and marshes, has shallow wells and level pools, and ample wood and pasture.

literal: Timber is taken at Huayin; overland transport seventy li;
idiomatic: Timber can be taken at Huayin and hauled overland seventy li;

literal: wood is cut at Longmen and floated downstream.
idiomatic: wood can be cut at Longmen and floated downstream.

literal: Trimming the old ramparts saves labor and strength; each man works for himself and does not count it hardship.
idiomatic: Trimming the old walls saves labor; each man works for himself and does not call it a burden.

literal: In former times the people of Song had no wells; they dug a well and rejoiced to gain a man;
idiomatic: Once the people of Song had no wells; they dug one and rejoiced to gain a man;

literal: how much more when a whole city had no water and, gaining water, would not celebrate in every household.
idiomatic: how much more when a whole city lacked water—would not every household celebrate once water came?

literal: I hear that former prefects were not without intent; sometimes troops were raised, sometimes years brought disaster—because of this the matter was left open and has been delayed until now.
idiomatic: I hear earlier prefects were not without the idea; war or famine always intervened, so the plan was set aside and has waited until now.

literal: Last year the harvest was ripe; this autumn the great crop is coming in; the four borders are calm and the capital has no trouble.
idiomatic: Last year's harvest was good; this autumn promises a great crop; the borders are quiet and the capital untroubled.

literal: Corvée costs less than ten cash per man; the people need no labor of eighty days.
idiomatic: Corvée will cost less than ten cash a man; the people need no eighty-day levy.

literal: To lighten the small and weight the great—I beg that your clear sight grant this.
idiomatic: A small cost for a great gain—I beg your clear sight to grant it.

literal: " Thereupon an edict said: "One effort for lasting ease—you may move as proposed.
idiomatic: " The throne answered: "One effort for lasting ease—move as you propose.

literal: " Later he was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Inspector of Bin Province.
idiomatic: " Later he was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Bin inspector.

literal: In the fourth year of Yanzhang he died.
idiomatic: He died in Yanzhang year 4.

literal: Posthumously given his former general's rank and made Inspector of Shuo.
idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his general's rank and was made Shuo inspector.

literal: Son: Chao
idiomatic: Son: Chao

literal: (With son: Xiaojing)
idiomatic: (Son: Xiaojing)

literal: His son Chao, style Huasheng.
idiomatic: His son Chao styled himself Huasheng.

literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he inherited.
idiomatic: When Suzong came to the throne he inherited.

literal: At that time because Hu Guozhen was enfeoffed Duke of Anding, he was changed to Prince of Beiping.
idiomatic: Because Hu Guozhen had been enfeoffed Duke of Anding, Chao was re-created Prince of Beiping.

literal: He was appointed Colonel of the City Gates, Regular Attendant in Direct Service, and General of the Eastern Gentlemen.
idiomatic: He was made colonel of the city gates, regular attendant in direct service, and general of the eastern gentlemen.

literal: Soon he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and took charge as Director of Palace Construction.
idiomatic: Soon he was Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and director of palace construction.

literal: Later his original enfeoffment was restored.
idiomatic: Later his original title was restored.

literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Chao fled to the south of Luo and met bandits and was killed.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Chao fled south of the Luo and was killed by bandits.

literal: [11] At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was posthumously made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, with Three Precedents parity, and Inspector of Qi.
idiomatic: [11] When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was posthumously General of the Chariots and Cavalry with Three Precedents parity and Qi inspector.

literal: His son Xiaojing inherited.
idiomatic: His son Xiaojing inherited.

literal: In Wuding he was Gentleman in Direct Service.
idiomatic: In Wuding he was gentleman in direct service.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Xie's younger brother: Yuanping
idiomatic: Xie's younger brother: Yuanping

literal: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was unrestrained and without conduct.
idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was wild and without conduct.

literal: At the end of Gaozu's reign he was appointed Outer Gentleman.
idiomatic: Late in Gaozu's reign he was made outer gentleman.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was promoted Attendant.
idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne he was promoted attendant.

literal: His perversity and wickedness grew daily; he killed men and robbed and plundered, becoming a scourge to public and private alike.
idiomatic: His perversity deepened daily—murder, robbery, plunder—until he scourged public and private life alike.

literal: Shizong, because he was a close kinsman, could not bear to bring him under the law; he was dismissed from office and confined in a separate lodge.
idiomatic: Shizong, as a near kinsman, could not bear to punish him by law; he was dismissed and shut in a separate lodge.

literal: The lodge was named Hall of Sorrowful Thought, in hope that he would restrain his thoughts.
idiomatic: The lodge was called the Hall of Sorrowful Thought, in hope he would check himself.

literal: When Shizong died, Yuanping was then able to come out.
idiomatic: When Shizong died, Yuanping was let out.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because his violence and disorder did not mend, an edict said: "Yuanping's will and conduct are light and scattered; he constantly violates the statutes—he may be returned to the separate lodge and confined as before.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling ruled, his violence still unabated, an edict said: "Yuanping's will and conduct are loose; he constantly breaks the law—return him to the separate lodge and confine him as before.

literal: " After a long while the confinement was lifted and he returned home, handed to tutors for strict admonition.
idiomatic: " After a long while the confinement was lifted; he went home under tutors who were to admonish him strictly.

literal: Later he was appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Service and Forward General.
idiomatic: Later he was regular attendant in direct service and forward general.

literal: He was convicted of stripping his wife Lady Wang naked before her sons and daughters, and of forcing himself on his wife's younger sister before his wife's mother.
idiomatic: He was convicted of stripping his wife Lady Wang naked before their children and of forcing his wife's younger sister before his mother-in-law.

literal: The Imperial Censor Hou Gang judged it unnatural conduct and sentenced him to death by strangulation; an amnesty spared him; he was demoted to Outer Attendant in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: Imperial censor Hou Gang tried him for unnatural conduct and sentenced him to strangulation; an amnesty spared him and he was demoted to outer attendant in ordinary service.

literal: In Xiaochang he died.
idiomatic: He died in Xiaochang.

literal: Son: Xu
idiomatic: Son: Xu

literal: (With son: Changchun, Prince of Nanjun)
idiomatic: (Son: Changchun, Prince of Nanjun)

literal: His son Xu, Recorder in the Anxi Office of You Province.
idiomatic: His son Xu was recorder in the Anxi office of You Province.

literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was Direct Attendant General.
idiomatic: When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was direct attendant general.

literal: Soon he was made with staff, acting Martial Guard General, and envoy comforting the twelve provinces west of the Pass; he then fell among the Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: Soon he was commissioned with staff as acting martial guard general and envoy comforting the twelve provinces west of the Pass; he then perished among the Tuyuhun.

literal: His son Changchun, Outer Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: His son Changchun was outer attendant at the palace secretariat in ordinary service.

literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanjun with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was created Prince of Nanjun with five hundred households.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Yuanping's younger brother: Yongping
idiomatic: Yuanping's younger brother: Yongping

literal: Yuanping's younger brother Yongping, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Inspector of Nan Province.
idiomatic: Yuanping's younger brother Yongping was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Nan inspector.

literal: [12] He was killed by the city man Hua Yanming.
idiomatic: [12] He was killed by a townsman, Hua Yanming.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given full staff, Palace Attendant, overall command of military affairs in Ding, Ying, and You provinces, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Ding.
idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously given full staff, palace attendant, overall command in Ding, Ying, and You, General of the Guard, and Ding inspector.

literal: Yongping's younger brother: Zhenping
idiomatic: Yongping's younger brother: Zhenping

literal: Yongping's younger brother Zhenping, Chief Clerk of Zhou Province.
idiomatic: Yongping's younger brother Zhenping was chief clerk of Zhou Province.

literal: Son: Shuzun
idiomatic: Son: Shuzun

literal: His son Shuzun, Outer Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: His son Shuzun was outer attendant at the palace secretariat in ordinary service.

literal: Zhenping's younger brother: Guiping
idiomatic: Zhenping's younger brother: Guiping

literal: Zhenping's younger brother Guiping, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, then Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot by Sound.
idiomatic: Zhenping's younger brother Guiping was supervisor of the feathered forest, then colonel of the archers who shoot by sound.

literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was made Regular Attendant and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed Prince of Donglai with a fief of one hundred households.
idiomatic: When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was regular attendant and vice director of the imperial clan, created Prince of Donglai with one hundred households.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Nanxiang Province.
idiomatic: He was General Who Pacifies the North and Nanxiang inspector.

literal: After Zhuangdi had killed Erzhu Rong he was further made Martial Guard General and concurrent Palace Attendant, and made envoy comforting Hebei and Shandong.
idiomatic: After Zhuangdi killed Erzhu Rong he was further martial guard general and concurrent palace attendant, and envoy comforting Hebei and Shandong.

literal: Reaching the northeast of Ding Province, he was seized by the Grand Commander of You Province Hou Yuan and sent to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Near northeast Ding he was seized by You grand commander Hou Yuan and sent to Jinyang.

literal: Later he returned to Luo.
idiomatic: Later he returned to Luoyang.

literal: In the time of the Former Deposed Emperor he held his former rank and handled affairs of Qing Province; the local man Cui Zuchi rebelled, the rebel band very strong, besieging Dongyang for more than a hundred days.
idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor he governed Qing with his former rank; the local strongman Cui Zuchi rebelled, his host was large, and Dongyang was besieged for more than a hundred days.

literal: Guiping led the townspeople in a firm defense and also ordered officers and soldiers to open the gates and give battle.
idiomatic: Guiping led the townspeople in a stubborn defense and ordered his officers to open the gates and fight.

literal: When the great army arrived in relief, Zuchi and the others were captured and beheaded.
idiomatic: When relief arrived, Zuchi and his fellows were taken and beheaded.

literal: On his return he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, further Regular Attendant, promoted Left Guard General and Director of the Imperial Clan, then promoted General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left, and Three Precedents parity.
idiomatic: On his return he was General of the Chariots and Cavalry with added regular attendant, then left guard general and director of the imperial clan, then again General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left, with Three Precedents parity.
